title: “Neumorphism and CSS”
lede: A March 2020 CSS-Tricks article that turned the style into CSS and set it against Material Design.
summary: Adrian Bece’s CSS-Tricks article: paired box-shadows, a comparison table with Material Design, and accessibility cautions.

evidence.note: Text read from the live page on 2026-09-28; the date is from its `article:published_time` metadata. Figures and demos were not inspected.

styles.note: A widely cited developer text that defines the style by its two shadows, one light and one dark, and by elements that share the background color.

context: The article says the style “got its name in a UX Collective post from December 2019” ([Malewicz](ref:malewicz-neumorphism-article-2019)) and that “Adam Giebl created an online generator for it” (neumorphism.io).

Its comparison table: in Material Design “elements have a single or multiple dark shadows around them”; in neumorphism “elements have two shadows: one light and one dark”. Background colors “must be the same (or very similar) as the background color of the parent element”, and “rounded edges are a defining quality”.

It allows an “optional subtle border to improve contrast”, and credits [Alexander Plyuto](ref:plyuto-skeuomorph-mobile-banking-2019) with having “championed and evolved neomorphic designs on his Dribbble account”.
interpretation: Evidence that by March 2020 the style had moved from Dribbble concepts into web practice, with CSS `box-shadow` pairs as its standard implementation.
